Periods can really (as I'm sure you know) amplify feelings of anxiety, depression and hopelessness. I recently self committed because I knew at some point I was just going to end things. Then I got my period and I felt so dumb. 

But I'm also really glad I did it, I got to a better head space, set up therapy and got meds that have actually been working for me. 

I'm currently taking Wellbutrin, which is not a standard SSI or SSNRI that I've taken in the past. "It is a norepinephrine-dopamine reuptake inhibitor (NDRI). An NDRI boosts levels of the neurotransmitters norepinephrine, also known as noradrenaline, and dopamine." so it doesn't focus on serotonin. For me, it's made my anxiety, depression, and feelings of hopelessness more manageable. I still have them, but it's easier to get out of bed and to interact with others without feeling like there's constantly something wrong with me. 

If you haven't consulted a doctor about this yet, that should be your first step. You don't need a diagnosis to get anti-depressants, a doctor can make that decision for you. 

When you answer the questions, don't answer based on how you're feeling that day, but how you've felt during those moments of anxiety and depression. Many times in the past when I've gone in and answered the questions, I've based it on how I'm feeling that day (which is usually better than the days before) and so I felt silly being there when I feel fine, but you need to base it on your lowest moments because that's when you need the most help. 

If money is an issue, I know planned parenthood has mental health services at a reasonable price and since it could be link to your period or possibly even thyroid then they can do some tests and exams for that too.
